bull_bear.body: The dilution question was pressed hard and answered directly. ~20% incremental equity issued to REA (5% already held from PropTiger), taking REA to 24.9%. The founder's defence: dilution "affects us personally the most… we think about this very deeply every time," and both dilutions went to REA specifically — "the largest PropTech group in the world," owned by News Corp — for the intangible of global learning. He noted that in earlier acquisitions "we never diluted, but we diluted to REA." Valuation discipline is the stronger argument: Housing at ~1.5x revenue against listed marketplace comparables at 4.5x-10x, and PropTiger at 1x revenue now effectively 0.5x after the turnaround. A promoter-subscribed **~INR 200 cr war chest** is being created as insurance — "it's just good to have funds in the company… but I don't envisage to use this."
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Housing.com's losses are large relative to Aurum.** ~INR 200 cr annualised burn against a company generating INR 2.31 cr of continuing-operations PBT per quarter. If the four-to-six-quarter clock slips, consolidated profitability reverses.
- **Listing platforms have structurally failed to be profitable in India** — an analyst pointed to 99acres losing money for years despite heavy spend. Management's counter is that it monetises *past* the listing, but that is an unproven model at Housing's scale.
- **The reported profit is small and the quarter's real profit came from an asset sale** (INR 52.40 cr PBT from discontinued operations vs INR 2.31 cr continuing).
- **Culture/integration risk**, raised bluntly by an analyst: Housing has had "several mercurial founders… no one has been really able to control this company and they have burned money a lot." Management's answer — that REA has stabilised it over recent years — is reasonable but does not address integration of a much larger organisation.
- **Dilution:** ~20% for an asset that currently loses money.
- **Seasonality is now structural to reported revenue** — PropTiger's slab-based brokerage means Q1 is weak and Q4 is strong by construction; QoQ comparisons will keep looking bad in H1.
- **Deal not closed** at the time of the call; tax structure, unit economics and firm guidance all deferred to Q3/H2.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, unusually specific with historical numbers, and willing to be pinned down. The most credible moment was the founder voluntarily disclosing the gap between the public and internal targets — "Our internal target is three to four quarters; we are today saying four to six quarters… let's take it four to six quarters" — which is under-promising made explicit. He answered the hostile questions directly: how much has been sunk into Housing (INR 2,200 cr, ~INR 1,000 cr on brand), what the burn is (INR 200 cr annualised), why dilute (REA specifically), and what the mercurial-founder history means. The framing "our challenge is not getting 1+1=2 and making that profitable; our challenge really is how to make 1+1=3" is honest about where the difficulty lies. Weaknesses: no numerical guidance on revenue or margins for two-to-three years, the acknowledged deferral of tax and unit-economics detail to H2, and a general vocabulary of ecosystem/flywheel language that outruns the INR 2.31 cr of continuing PBT.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The quarter's profit is not the quarter's profit.** INR 52.40 cr of PBT came from discontinued operations (building sale); continuing operations delivered INR 2.31 cr. The margin expansion is real, but the absolute profit is thin.
- **The QoQ revenue decline is a feature of the PropTiger contract structure**, not deterioration — annual operating plans unlock progressively higher brokerage slabs, so value crystallises in H2/Q4. Expect this shape every year.
- **Aurum bought the one thing it could not build.** Everything downstream (Analytica for enterprise, Sell.do and Analytica for brokers, NestAway for living) already existed; what was missing was the earliest discovery signal, which only Google-scale search or a marketplace can capture.
- **The comparables argument is the real valuation defence** — 1.5x revenue against 4.5x-10x for listed Indian marketplaces, and a PropTiger precedent where 1x became an effective 0.5x post-turnaround.
- **REA sold the asset but took 24.9% of the acquirer** — as the founder put it, "it is not an exit which only fetches INR 458 crores… they have now 24.9% in the largest PropTech company in the country." REA is betting on the integration succeeding, which is a meaningful alignment signal.
- Housing follows a **July-June (ASX) financial calendar**, so its FY26 audited numbers will not align with Aurum's reporting for some time.

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Enterprise risk oversight is new and voluntary rather than mandated — The Company describes a 'voluntarily structured Group Risk Management Framework', and its Risk Management Committee was constituted only on January 19, 2026 - late in FY 2025-26. The committee's remit names the risk classes management itself flags as material: Strategic and Commercial risks including Cybersecurity, Safety and Operations, Compliance, Control and Financial risks. A framework and committee that young have limited operating track record.
- Cybersecurity and data risk in a platform holding consumer and developer data — Cybersecurity is named explicitly among the material risks the Risk Management Committee must ensure are identified and assessed. The business model - a unified digital ecosystem with a proprietary data lake, AI lead scoring and 25,000+ active customers plus 1,100+ developer relationships - concentrates sensitive personal and transaction data on the platform, so a breach is a structural, not incidental, exposure.
- The strategy is levered to AI execution whose payoff is deferred — Management states the AI stack is live across all five product platforms but that 'the full strategic impact of these deployments expected to reflect in 2026-27 performance', and the quantified benefits (30% lower customer acquisition cost, 20% higher lead conversion, 80% lower ticket resolution time) are labelled 'Potential Business Impact'. If those benefits do not land, the operating-leverage case for FY 2026-27 weakens with no disclosed fallback.
- Acquisition and integration risk concentrated in PropTiger — PropTiger was acquired 100% mid-year (reporting period from September 26, 2025) through an all-stock equity swap for Rs 8,645.00 lakhs, funded by issuing 42,42,537 new equity shares - so shareholders bore dilution and brought REA Group in as a strategic shareholder. Distribution is described as the primary growth and profitability engine, and its migration onto the in-house Sell.Do technology stack is still 'ongoing', leaving integration execution as an open risk on the segment carrying the growth case.
- Profitability remains marginal at the consolidated level — The Company's own FY 2025-26 Performance Highlights show a PBT margin of (2.9%) and adjusted EBITDA of 5.9% - i.e. the group is still loss-making before tax on a reported basis even after a year described as a structural inflection. There is little cushion if any one vertical deteriorates.
- Complex, shifting group structure with control changes and step-down entities — The entity map changed materially in one year: Integrow ceased to be a subsidiary from June 30, 2025 with board control transferred to external investors and is now a 48.54% associate, with the Company's majority-control right kept in abeyance until March 31, 2027; two wholly owned subsidiaries were merged; the K2V2 stake rose to 90.14%; and new overseas entities (NestAway PropTech Mena Real Estate L.L.C in AED, Monk Tech Labs Pte. Limited in USD) were consolidated. Frequent consolidation-perimeter changes make period-on-period comparability and control assessment harder.
- Related-party financial support flowing to and from the promoter group — Form AOC-2 discloses an approved arrangement to provide financial assistance in one or more tranches to Aurum RealEstate Developers Limited, the Promoter Company, and an unsecured loan facility from the Company to wholly owned subsidiary NestAway Technologies, both spanning FY 2025-26 and FY 2026-27. The Board states these are at arm's length and that there were no materially significant related-party transactions with potential conflict, but funding a promoter entity is a structural governance watch-item.
- Reduced mandatory disclosure and no external credit assessment — BRSR is not applicable to the Company under Regulation 34 of the SEBI Listing Regulations; CSR provisions were not applicable for FY 2025-26 because the Company did not satisfy the Section 135(1) criteria; and the Company obtained no credit ratings during the year. Investors therefore have neither a standardised sustainability disclosure nor a third-party credit opinion to triangulate against management's own account.
- Macro and geopolitical drag on capital flows — The Chairman's message flags that the global economy is projected to moderate from 3.4% growth in 2025 to 3.2% by 2027, with the Russia-Ukraine conflict, Middle East trade-route disruption and intensifying US-China rivalry continuing to weigh on global trade and investment flows - relevant to a business whose Capital vertical depends on institutional and individual investment appetite for Indian real estate.
- Forward-looking statements carry acknowledged assumption risk — The Company's own disclaimer states there is 'a significant risk that the assumptions, predictions, and other forward-looking statements may not prove to be accurate' and cautions readers against undue reliance - a material caveat given how much of this AR's investment case is stated as future AI-driven outcomes rather than delivered results.

business.body:
- **Rental (INR 54.35 cr, profit INR 0.63 cr):** HelloWorld co-living, NestAway managed rentals, student housing and family rentals across 21 cities. **Both rental businesses achieved EBITDA profitability** — the stated milestone. Strategy is occupancy, tenant experience and operational efficiency "rather than simply expanding inventory."
- **Distribution (INR 55.94 cr, profit INR 7.97 cr):** Aurum Analytica (lead intelligence), Sell.do (SaaS CRM), PropTiger (brokerage). The profit engine, and always profitable.

- **Housing.com (to be acquired):** marketplace model serving three customer types — developers, channel partners, and DIY consumers. - **PropTiger:** acquired from REA in July 2025 at ~1x revenue for INR 84 cr of shares; was loss-making, turned around, and has now delivered its **first two quarters of profitability** — the proof-point management leans on.

outlook.body:
- **The monetisation thesis:** "Traditionally, property portals monetize listings and advertisements; our monetization begins when the portals end." Housing.com captures consumer intent; Aurum monetises it through developer technology, transaction fulfilment, rentals, financing and AI-enabled services across the whole consumer journey — expanding consumer lifetime value and capturing a larger share of each transaction's economics.
- **Three named revenue levers on Housing:** (1) convert intent-monetisation into transaction-monetisation across developers, brokers and DIY; (2) upsell existing Housing product SKUs, which management says have good tech but "minimal utilisation"; (3) ancillary cross-sell — Housing × PropTiger, Housing × Sell.do, Housing × NestAway/HelloWorld.
- **AI across five layers** — Discovery, Intelligence, Transaction, Financing, Living — with **revenue per team member** as the tracked productivity metric. Medium-term goal is "Aurum's Unified Brain," a single intelligence layer activating monetisation across the ecosystem.
- **Industry consolidation:** "Aurum's acquisition of Housing.com marks the start of industry-wide consolidation in Indian PropTech, and at Aurum, we intend to lead it."
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Move from assembly to integration: connect the previously separate rental, distribution and capital platforms into a single operating architecture bringing data, workflows and transactions together - the Chairman frames FY 2025-26 as the year that shift happened and FY 2026-27 as the year focus turns 'from building to scaling'.
- Become AI-first: embed an agentic AI architecture into the core of the ecosystem across rentals, distribution and capital, moving AI from experimentation to adoption, with the stated ambition to 'define how intelligence becomes the operating system of the RealEstate ecosystem'.
- Build a 'Unified Brain' - an intelligence layer integrating data, workflows and platform capabilities that continuously learns and connects intelligence across the businesses to enable faster decisions.
- Deploy AI across four named themes: AI-Powered Sales Acceleration (intelligent voice agents for lead qualification and automated site-visit scheduling), AI-driven Marketing Intelligence (hyper-personalized campaigns, SEO and Answer Engine Optimization), a Predictive Conversion Engine (behavioral analytics, AI-led lead scoring, intent-based recommendations) and Autonomous Customer Experience (chatbots, automated ticket management, AI co-pilots).

outlook.body: Aurum PropTech is an asset-light PropTech platform, so expansion is expressed as footprint, inventory and platform build-out rather than plant capex. Rental footprint: the rental business, run through HelloWorld (co-living) and NestAway (family rentals), is described as the largest organized player by managed inventory with 28,000+ units across 15 cities and a stated rental capacity of 28,800+ units; HelloWorld scaled during FY 2025-26 to 270+ properties and approximately 19,800 beds while maintaining occupancy above 74%. FY 2025-26 was a deliberate pivot from growth-at-any-cost to profitability-led, hyper-local market leadership, so expansion was partly negative: NestAway strategically off-boarded underperforming inventory, particularly across select student housing and high-cost micro-markets, which improved EBITDA margins, while its expansion into secondary home sales opened a new revenue stream with strong early traction. Geographic expansion: the Company launched Nestr in Dubai during the year, its first international market, described as demonstrating the portability and scalability of its tech-enabled rental model beyond India. Inorganic expansion: the Company completed the acquisition of 100% of PropTiger Marketing Services India Private Limited from REA India Pte. Limited, Singapore through an all-stock equity swap for an aggregate consideration of Rs 8,645.00 lakhs (42,42,537 equity shares of face value Rs 5 issued at Rs 203.77 per share), making PropTiger a wholly owned subsidiary; approved acquisition of up to 8.2% additional equity in K2V2 Technologies for consideration not exceeding Rs 633.00 lakhs, taking its holding to 90.14%; disinvested 0.60% of Integrow Asset Management and kept majority-control rights on Integrow's board in abeyance until March 31, 2027; and approved a Scheme of Merger amalgamating wholly owned subsidiary Aurum Softwares and Solutions into Liv Real Solutions under Section 233 of the Companies Act, 2013 (board approval March 02, 2026, shareholder approval March 13, 2026). Platform build-out: the principal 'capex' theme is an AI and automation programme - an agentic AI architecture and a 'Unified Brain' intelligence layer being embedded across rentals, distribution and capital, with AI deployed in production across lead management, sales intelligence, customer support and operational workflows. The AR discloses no manufacturing plants, no installed plant capacity and no rupee capital-expenditure quantum.

outlook.body:
- Sector digital adoption: the Indian PropTech market is projected to expand from USD 20 billion in CY25 to USD 87.61 billion by CY30, a 34% CAGR, reflecting the growing role of technology across the RealEstate value chain.
- Rental supply gap: demand of ~2.04 crore units against organized supply of ~9 lakhs (a 23x gap), with an estimated market size of USD 26 billion by 2030 - management's take is that the primary opportunity lies in formalizing and scaling rental supply through technology.
- Rental sub-segment demand: student housing (~41 lakh students vs <3 lakh organized units), young professionals / co-living (~67 lakh demand vs <4 lakh units in major cities) and family rentals (~1.01 crore households vs <1 lakh organized listings).
- Distribution digitization: >90% of buyers use digital channels to search homes, 60% use virtual tours before buying, 58% of sales and marketing budget is spent on digital strategies and 75% of channel partners use technology tools - with developer spend of Rs 1,000 crore on aggregator websites, Rs 4,000 crore on social media and Rs 34,000 crore on channel sales; the stated addressable market is Rs 39,000 crore.
- Key distribution drivers named: AI-led demand aggregation, digital broker ecosystems, and virtual tours with omnichannel sales; the principal opportunity is building end-to-end digital transaction platforms that consolidate a historically fragmented market.
- Capital: the SM-REIT structure opens India's income-generating commercial RealEstate segment to a broader investor base, with Rs 50,000+ crore of SM-REIT-able supply, 300 family offices with average AUM of USD 100 million looking for alpha income diversification, and Rs 561 billion of net inflows by individual investors.
- Macro backdrop: the global economy grew 3.4% in 2025 and is projected to moderate to 3.2% by 2027 amid geopolitical uncertainty, while India's GDP is projected to expand by 7.7% in FY 2025-26 on strong domestic consumption, improving rural demand, stable inflation and sustained public and private investment; AI has emerged as a major catalyst for capital allocation globally.
- Operating leverage narrative: transforming PropTech from fragmented digital tools to an intelligent operating ecosystem is expected to deepen customer experience, improve operating leverage, strengthen platform scalability and deliver measurable business outcomes.

deepdive.thesis: Two stories in one quarter: a third consecutive profitable quarter with PBT margins up 1,590 bps and adjusted EBITDA margins up 1,320 bps on total income of INR 119-121 cr (+57-61% YoY) — and the announced acquisition of **Housing.com**, India's #1 consumer real-estate brand (24% online-portal share, 58 mn monthly visits) which is currently burning **INR 200 cr a year** and whose FY25 expenses (INR 531 cr) exceeded revenue (INR 343 cr) by INR 188 cr. Aurum is paying ~1.5x revenue in equity (~20% incremental dilution to REA Group) and publicly committing to break Housing even in **four to six quarters** — against an internal target of three to four. The entire investment case now rests on whether the NestAway/PropTiger turnaround playbook scales to an asset five times larger.

one-line thesis: Two stories in one quarter: a third consecutive profitable quarter with PBT margins up 1,590 bps and adjusted EBITDA margins up 1,320 bps on total income of INR 119-121 cr (+57-61% YoY) — and the announced acquisition of **Housing.com**, India's #1 consumer real-estate brand (24% online-portal share, 58 mn monthly visits) which is currently burning **INR 200 cr a year** and whose FY25 expenses (INR 531 cr) exceeded revenue (INR 343 cr) by INR 188 cr. Aurum is paying ~1.5x revenue in equity (~20% incremental dilution to REA Group) and publicly committing to break Housing even in **four to six quarters** — against an internal target of three to four. growth verticals / optionality:
- **The monetisation thesis:** "Traditionally, property portals monetize listings and advertisements; our monetization begins when the portals end." Housing.com captures consumer intent; Aurum monetises it through developer technology, transaction fulfilment, rentals, financing and AI-enabled services across the whole consumer journey — expanding consumer lifetime value and capturing a larger share of each transaction's economics.
- **Three named revenue levers on Housing:** (1) convert intent-monetisation into transaction-monetisation across developers, brokers and DIY; (2) upsell existing Housing product SKUs, which management says have good tech but "minimal utilisation"; (3) ancillary cross-sell — Housing × PropTiger, Housing × Sell.do, Housing × NestAway/HelloWorld.
- **AI across five layers** — Discovery, Intelligence, Transaction, Financing, Living — with **revenue per team member** as the tracked productivity metric. Medium-term goal is "Aurum's Unified Brain," a single intelligence layer activating monetisation across the ecosystem.
- **Industry consolidation:** "Aurum's acquisition of Housing.com marks the start of industry-wide consolidation in Indian PropTech, and at Aurum, we intend to lead it."
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **The only end-to-end stack in Indian PropTech** post-Housing: discovery/listing → lead intelligence → CRM → brokerage → managed living → financing. The specific gap Housing closes is **top-of-funnel intent** — "the intent at the earliest stage of property discovery, which only two internet platforms get, one is of course the likes of Google… and second is marketplace platforms like Housing."
- **Brand asset acquired below replacement cost:** ~INR 2,200 cr has been invested into Housing over 14-15 years, of which ~INR 1,000 cr went into the brand. Aurum acquired at ~1.5x revenue against listed Indian marketplace comparables at 4.5x and, in one case, 10x revenue.
- **A demonstrated turnaround playbook:** NestAway (worse revenue-to-loss ratio than Housing, turned around), PropTiger (acquired at 1x revenue, two profitable quarters, effective dilution now ~0.5x), HelloWorld. Management's stated edge over tech-built businesses: "businesses that are built by tech teams… do lack that understanding on the real estate practice side."
- **Sell.do stickiness:** 7% gross churn with licences and developer count growing.
- **REA Group as a 24.9% shareholder** — the world's largest PropTech group, owned by News Corp — described as a source of global learning rather than just capital.
margins & cost dynamics: PBT margin +1,590 bps and adjusted EBITDA margin +1,320 bps YoY, and management insists "these improvements are not the result of one-off cost actions; they are being driven by stronger business fundamentals, improved productivity, and disciplined capital allocation." Notably margins improved **1,000+ bps despite Q1 being "the industry's softest quarter."** The forward cost programme on Housing is specific: (a) internationally-invested, corporately-managed businesses "typically become management-heavy, top-heavy" versus Aurum's lean structure with frontline empowerment; (b) sales-team right-sizing on the broker and developer sides; (c) marketing efficiency — better use of credits on Meta, other social platforms and Google, disciplining performance/brand/SC expenditure; (d) working-capital discipline to cap expenditure. Aurum will also extend Analytica and Sell.do's enterprise team learnings into Housing.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Asset-light by design — capital goes into AI infrastructure rather than physical assets, and the rental strategy explicitly de-prioritises inventory expansion in favour of occupancy and efficiency. The one physical event was a **disposal**: the sale of a company-owned building for INR 112 cr. The expansion this quarter is entirely inorganic (Housing.com) and organisational (AI embedding). The slippage risks to watch are the **transaction close** (not yet completed at the time of the call — repeated references to "once we approach more towards the closing") and the **four-to-six-quarter breakeven clock**, which only starts on close.
capital allocation: The dilution question was pressed hard and answered directly. ~20% incremental equity issued to REA (5% already held from PropTiger), taking REA to 24.9%. The founder's defence: dilution "affects us personally the most… we think about this very deeply every time," and both dilutions went to REA specifically — "the largest PropTech group in the world," owned by News Corp — for the intangible of global learning. He noted that in earlier acquisitions "we never diluted, but we diluted to REA." Valuation discipline is the stronger argument: Housing at ~1.5x revenue against listed marketplace comparables at 4.5x-10x, and PropTiger at 1x revenue now effectively 0.5x after the turnaround. A promoter-subscribed **~INR 200 cr war chest** is being created as insurance — "it's just good to have funds in the company… but I don't envisage to use this."
risks & watch-items:
- **Housing.com's losses are large relative to Aurum.** ~INR 200 cr annualised burn against a company generating INR 2.31 cr of continuing-operations PBT per quarter. If the four-to-six-quarter clock slips, consolidated profitability reverses.
- **Listing platforms have structurally failed to be profitable in India** — an analyst pointed to 99acres losing money for years despite heavy spend. Management's counter is that it monetises *past* the listing, but that is an unproven model at Housing's scale.
- **The reported profit is small and the quarter's real profit came from an asset sale** (INR 52.40 cr PBT from discontinued operations vs INR 2.31 cr continuing).
- **Culture/integration risk**, raised bluntly by an analyst: Housing has had "several mercurial founders… no one has been really able to control this company and they have burned money a lot." Management's answer — that REA has stabilised it over recent years — is reasonable but does not address integration of a much larger organisation.
- **Dilution:** ~20% for an asset that currently loses money.
- **Seasonality is now structural to reported revenue** — PropTiger's slab-based brokerage means Q1 is weak and Q4 is strong by construction; QoQ comparisons will keep looking bad in H1.
- **Deal not closed** at the time of the call; tax structure, unit economics and firm guidance all deferred to Q3/H2.
management quality / tone: Confident, unusually specific with historical numbers, and willing to be pinned down. The most credible moment was the founder voluntarily disclosing the gap between the public and internal targets — "Our internal target is three to four quarters; we are today saying four to six quarters… let's take it four to six quarters" — which is under-promising made explicit. He answered the hostile questions directly: how much has been sunk into Housing (INR 2,200 cr, ~INR 1,000 cr on brand), what the burn is (INR 200 cr annualised), why dilute (REA specifically), and what the mercurial-founder history means. The framing "our challenge is not getting 1+1=2 and making that profitable; our challenge really is how to make 1+1=3" is honest about where the difficulty lies. Weaknesses: no numerical guidance on revenue or margins for two-to-three years, the acknowledged deferral of tax and unit-economics detail to H2, and a general vocabulary of ecosystem/flywheel language that outruns the INR 2.31 cr of continuing PBT.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The quarter's profit is not the quarter's profit.** INR 52.40 cr of PBT came from discontinued operations (building sale); continuing operations delivered INR 2.31 cr. The margin expansion is real, but the absolute profit is thin.
- **The QoQ revenue decline is a feature of the PropTiger contract structure**, not deterioration — annual operating plans unlock progressively higher brokerage slabs, so value crystallises in H2/Q4. Expect this shape every year.
- **Aurum bought the one thing it could not build.** Everything downstream (Analytica for enterprise, Sell.do and Analytica for brokers, NestAway for living) already existed; what was missing was the earliest discovery signal, which only Google-scale search or a marketplace can capture.
- **The comparables argument is the real valuation defence** — 1.5x revenue against 4.5x-10x for listed Indian marketplaces, and a PropTiger precedent where 1x became an effective 0.5x post-turnaround.
- **REA sold the asset but took 24.9% of the acquirer** — as the founder put it, "it is not an exit which only fetches INR 458 crores… they have now 24.9% in the largest PropTech company in the country." REA is betting on the integration succeeding, which is a meaningful alignment signal.
- Housing follows a **July-June (ASX) financial calendar**, so its FY26 audited numbers will not align with Aurum's reporting for some time.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **The monetisation thesis:** "Traditionally, property portals monetize listings and advertisements; our monetization begins when the portals end." Housing.com captures consumer intent; Aurum monetises it through developer technology, transaction fulfilment, rentals, financing and AI-enabled services across the whole consumer journey — expanding consumer lifetime value and capturing a larger share of each transaction's economics.
- **Three named revenue levers on Housing:** (1) convert intent-monetisation into transaction-monetisation across developers, brokers and DIY; (2) upsell existing Housing product SKUs, which management says have good tech but "minimal utilisation"; (3) ancillary cross-sell — Housing × PropTiger, Housing × Sell.do, Housing × NestAway/HelloWorld.
- **AI across five layers** — Discovery, Intelligence, Transaction, Financing, Living — with **revenue per team member** as the tracked productivity metric. Medium-term goal is "Aurum's Unified Brain," a single intelligence layer activating monetisation across the ecosystem.
- **Industry consolidation:** "Aurum's acquisition of Housing.com marks the start of industry-wide consolidation in Indian PropTech, and at Aurum, we intend to lead it."

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Sector digital adoption: the Indian PropTech market is projected to expand from USD 20 billion in CY25 to USD 87.61 billion by CY30, a 34% CAGR, reflecting the growing role of technology across the RealEstate value chain.
- Rental supply gap: demand of ~2.04 crore units against organized supply of ~9 lakhs (a 23x gap), with an estimated market size of USD 26 billion by 2030 - management's take is that the primary opportunity lies in formalizing and scaling rental supply through technology.
- Rental sub-segment demand: student housing (~41 lakh students vs <3 lakh organized units), young professionals / co-living (~67 lakh demand vs <4 lakh units in major cities) and family rentals (~1.01 crore households vs <1 lakh organized listings).
- Distribution digitization: >90% of buyers use digital channels to search homes, 60% use virtual tours before buying, 58% of sales and marketing budget is spent on digital strategies and 75% of channel partners use technology tools - with developer spend of Rs 1,000 crore on aggregator websites, Rs 4,000 crore on social media and Rs 34,000 crore on channel sales; the stated addressable market is Rs 39,000 crore.
- Key distribution drivers named: AI-led demand aggregation, digital broker ecosystems, and virtual tours with omnichannel sales; the principal opportunity is building end-to-end digital transaction platforms that consolidate a historically fragmented market.
- Capital: the SM-REIT structure opens India's income-generating commercial RealEstate segment to a broader investor base, with Rs 50,000+ crore of SM-REIT-able supply, 300 family offices with average AUM of USD 100 million looking for alpha income diversification, and Rs 561 billion of net inflows by individual investors.
- Macro backdrop: the global economy grew 3.4% in 2025 and is projected to moderate to 3.2% by 2027 amid geopolitical uncertainty, while India's GDP is projected to expand by 7.7% in FY 2025-26 on strong domestic consumption, improving rural demand, stable inflation and sustained public and private investment; AI has emerged as a major catalyst for capital allocation globally.
- Operating leverage narrative: transforming PropTech from fragmented digital tools to an intelligent operating ecosystem is expected to deepen customer experience, improve operating leverage, strengthen platform scalability and deliver measurable business outcomes.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: PBT margin +1,590 bps and adjusted EBITDA margin +1,320 bps YoY, and management insists "these improvements are not the result of one-off cost actions; they are being driven by stronger business fundamentals, improved productivity, and disciplined capital allocation." Notably margins improved **1,000+ bps despite Q1 being "the industry's softest quarter."** The forward cost programme on Housing is specific: (a) internationally-invested, corporately-managed businesses "typically become management-heavy, top-heavy" versus Aurum's lean structure with frontline empowerment; (b) sales-team right-sizing on the broker and developer sides; (c) marketing efficiency — better use of credits on Meta, other social platforms and Google, disciplining performance/brand/SC expenditure; (d) working-capital discipline to cap expenditure. capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: The dilution question was pressed hard and answered directly. ~20% incremental equity issued to REA (5% already held from PropTiger), taking REA to 24.9%. The founder's defence: dilution "affects us personally the most… we think about this very deeply every time," and both dilutions went to REA specifically — "the largest PropTech group in the world," owned by News Corp — for the intangible of global learning. capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Aurum PropTech is an asset-light PropTech platform, so expansion is expressed as footprint, inventory and platform build-out rather than plant capex. Rental footprint: the rental business, run through HelloWorld (co-living) and NestAway (family rentals), is described as the largest organized player by managed inventory with 28,000+ units across 15 cities and a stated rental capacity of 28,800+ units; HelloWorld scaled during FY 2025-26 to 270+ properties and approximately 19,800 beds while maintaining occupancy above 74%. FY 2025-26 was a deliberate pivot from growth-at-any-cost to profitability-led, hyper-local market leadership, so expansion was partly negative: NestAway strategically off-boarded underperforming inventory, particularly across select student housing and high-cost micro-markets, which improved EBITDA margins, while its expansion into secondary home sales opened a new revenue stream with strong early traction. Geographic expansion: the Company launched Nestr in Dubai during the year, its first international market, described as demonstrating the portability and scalability of its tech-enabled rental model beyond India. Inorganic expansion: the Company completed the acquisition of 100% of PropTiger Marketing Services India Private Limited from REA India Pte. Limited, Singapore through an all-stock equity swap for an aggregate consideration of Rs 8,645.00 lakhs (42,42,537 equity shares of face value Rs 5 issued at Rs 203.77 per share), making PropTiger a wholly owned subsidiary; approved acquisition of up to 8.2% additional equity in K2V2 Technologies for consideration not exceeding Rs 633.00 lakhs, taking its holding to 90.14%; disinvested 0.60% of Integrow Asset Management and kept majority-control rights on Integrow's board in abeyance until March 31, 2027; and approved a Scheme of Merger amalgamating wholly owned subsidiary Aurum Softwares and Solutions into Liv Real Solutions under Section 233 of the Companies Act, 2013 (board approval March 02, 2026, shareholder approval March 13, 2026). management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, unusually specific with historical numbers, and willing to be pinned down. risks.title: Risks & watch-items

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- **The quarter's profit is not the quarter's profit.** INR 52.40 cr of PBT came from discontinued operations (building sale); continuing operations delivered INR 2.31 cr. The margin expansion is real, but the absolute profit is thin.
- **The QoQ revenue decline is a feature of the PropTiger contract structure**, not deterioration — annual operating plans unlock progressively higher brokerage slabs, so value crystallises in H2/Q4. Expect this shape every year.
- **Aurum bought the one thing it could not build.** Everything downstream (Analytica for enterprise, Sell.do and Analytica for brokers, NestAway for living) already existed; what was missing was the earliest discovery signal, which only Google-scale search or a marketplace can capture.
- **The comparables argument is the real valuation defence** — 1.5x revenue against 4.5x-10x for listed Indian marketplaces, and a PropTiger precedent where 1x became an effective 0.5x post-turnaround.
- **REA sold the asset but took 24.9% of the acquirer** — as the founder put it, "it is not an exit which only fetches INR 458 crores… they have now 24.9% in the largest PropTech company in the country." REA is betting on the integration succeeding, which is a meaningful alignment signal.

- **Deal not closed** at the time of the call; tax structure, unit economics and firm guidance all deferred to Q3/H2.
management quality / tone: Confident, unusually specific with historical numbers, and willing to be pinned down. The most credible moment was the founder voluntarily disclosing the gap between the public and internal targets — "Our internal target is three to four quarters; we are today saying four to six quarters… let's take it four to six quarters" — which is under-promising made explicit. He answered the hostile questions directly: how much has been sunk into Housing (INR 2,200 cr, ~INR 1,000 cr on brand), what the burn is (INR 200 cr annualised), why dilute (REA specifically), and what the mercurial-founder history means. The framing "our challenge is not getting 1+1=2 and making that profitable; our challenge really is how to make 1+1=3" is honest about where the difficulty lies. Weaknesses: no numerical guidance on revenue or margins for two-to-three years, the acknowledged deferral of tax and unit-economics detail to H2, and a general vocabulary of ecosystem/flywheel language that outruns the INR 2.31 cr of continuing PBT.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The quarter's profit is not the quarter's profit.** INR 52.40 cr of PBT came from discontinued operations (building sale); continuing operations delivered INR 2.31 cr. The margin expansion is real, but the absolute profit is thin.
- **The QoQ revenue decline is a feature of the PropTiger contract structure**, not deterioration — annual operating plans unlock progressively higher brokerage slabs, so value crystallises in H2/Q4. Expect this shape every year.
- **Aurum bought the one thing it could not build.** Everything downstream (Analytica for enterprise, Sell.do and Analytica for brokers, NestAway for living) already existed; what was missing was the earliest discovery signal, which only Google-scale search or a marketplace can capture.
- **The comparables argument is the real valuation defence** — 1.5x revenue against 4.5x-10x for listed Indian marketplaces, and a PropTiger precedent where 1x became an effective 0.5x post-turnaround.
- **REA sold the asset but took 24.9% of the acquirer** — as the founder put it, "it is not an exit which only fetches INR 458 crores… they have now 24.9% in the largest PropTech company in the country." REA is betting on the integration succeeding, which is a meaningful alignment signal.
- Housing follows a **July-June (ASX) financial calendar**, so its FY26 audited numbers will not align with Aurum's reporting for some time.
